Builder carries them as requirements: export invariant (data-iv-export-css and EXPORT_SVG unchanged), live test accepts google-chrome, chromium and chromium-browser, backward-compat note lists the new .insrc-viewer CSS rules, c3-c5 linked from the body.

summary.prose: Generated mock, UML and ER pages and the docgen pages now apply the light or dark mode to the whole browser document, including the margin and the area below short content, open in light unless the reader has chosen otherwise, and no longer show the font data as text at the top. The theme switch becomes a small floating button fixed at the top right of the page, with room reserved above the content so it never covers the header at the top of the page. The companion page puts its theme root on the body as the docgen pages already do, so one set of page rules serves all three shells; the degraded docgen page keeps its own small script.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Apply the artifact page theme to the whole document, default to light and float the switch top right; also stop the packaged font-face CSS from showing as text at the top of the page

parameters.name: structuralCss
parameters.purpose: The shell's own layout CSS, appended to both mode style tags.

api.name: pageCssFor

parameters.name: mode
parameters.purpose: The surface mode, light or dark.

returns.meaning: The page surface CSS for the mode.

postconditions: '.insrc-viewer' (the body in every shell) carries the surface background and colour, 'box-sizing:border-box', 'min-height:100vh' and 'padding-top:56px', so it fills the viewport with room above the content for the floating switch

No rule gives html a background of its own, so the body background propagates to the whole canvas (core CSS canvas propagation, no :has() or other newer selector) and no white strip shows below short content or in the overscroll area
Contains a rule that makes '.insrc-viewer #iv-theme' a fixed-position 32px control at top:12px and right:12px with a z-index above the page content, readable in both modes
Every rule is still scoped under .insrc-viewer

api.name: viewerBootScript

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: Initial mode and the Mermaid config per mode.

returns.meaning: The inline boot script that selects and applies the mode.

preconditions: The page has an element with class insrc-viewer that is the theme root
postconditions: The mode is the stored insrc-theme-mode when it is light or dark, otherwise opts.initialMode; the operating system's colour-scheme preference is not consulted
A throwing localStorage is caught in each of the two try blocks (the read and the write in applyMode) and the mode falls back to opts.initialMode
The mode is applied to the .insrc-viewer root, which in every shell is the body, and a missing #iv-theme element is tolerated

dataModelChanges.details: The key and its two values are unchanged. The invariant that changes: with no stored value the page opens in light, where before it opened in the operating system's preferred mode. A stored value still wins. No new entity and no relationship change, so no ER definition is needed; the floating control is a single fixed-position button, so no UX mock is needed.

errorCases.response: The read falls back to the initial mode, light; the write is skipped; the toggle still works for the session
errorCases.userImpact: The page opens in light and the choice is not remembered

errorCases.scenario: The stored value is neither light nor dark
errorCases.detection: The boot script checks the stored value against the two allowed values before using it
errorCases.response: It is ignored and the page opens in light
errorCases.userImpact: None; the page opens in the default

errorCases.scenario: The page has no #iv-theme element (a page built without the control)
errorCases.detection: applyMode and the click wiring test the element before using it, as the existing code does
errorCases.response: The mode still applies from storage or the default; there is simply no button

testLevels.purpose: ac1: the mode applies to the whole document. In every shell the body is the .insrc-viewer theme root carrying data-theme and the export CSS. pageCssFor, in both modes, gives '.insrc-viewer' the surface background, 'min-height:100vh', 'box-sizing:border-box' and 'padding-top:56px', no rule gives html a background of its own, and docgenPageStyle no longer holds the never-matching '.insrc-viewer html,.insrc-viewer body' rule. ac2: with no stored choice the page opens in light and the colour-scheme preference is not consulted, in the boot script and in the fallback shell's own script, and the fallback script uses the same storage key and default as the shared one; a stored light or dark value still wins. The boot script is also run against a stub DOM for a throwing localStorage read, a throwing write, an invalid stored value and a missing #iv-theme. ac3: the font-face rules are inside a <style> element and the companion layout rule '.insrc-viewer .page' can match. ac4: #iv-theme is a direct child of the body, outside the toolbars, in the companion, docgen and fallback pages, and the page CSS makes it a fixed 32px top-right control above the content; the companion CSS has the max-width:480px rule that stacks the header and lets table.ref shrink.

migration.stateBefore: A companion page puts the mode on a div inside the body, so html and body have no background and show white around dark pages and below short content; no rule makes the theme root fill the viewport or reserves room for a floating control; every page opens in dark when the operating system prefers dark and no choice is stored; every page shows the packaged font-face CSS as text because pageStyleTags adds it without a style tag; the companion layout rule '.insrc-viewer .page' never matches; the companion header table has a 380px minimum width; the docgen shell carries a '.insrc-viewer html,.insrc-viewer body' rule that can never match; and the theme button sits inside the toolbar of each shell (src/artifact-theme/theme.ts:271-316, src/artifact-theme/theme.ts:361-461, src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts:166-269, src/docgen/render/shell.ts:203-273, src/docgen/render/fallback.ts:240-287).
migration.stateAfter: In every shell the body is the theme root, fills the viewport, reserves 56px above the content and paints the whole canvas through background propagation, so the mode reaches the whole document; with no stored choice a page opens in light; the font-face rules sit inside a style element; the companion layout rule matches and its header table fits a 360px viewport; the dead docgen rule is gone; and the theme button is a fixed 32px top-right control that is a direct child of the body.

migrationSteps.action: Wrap the font-face rules in a style element, drop the operating-system preference from the boot script and from the fallback shell's own script, and add to the shared page CSS the body fill and top clearance and the fixed top-right rule for the theme switch; update the shared theme tests, including the stub-DOM boot script tests; commit.

Move the theme root to the body in the companion shell, add its narrow-width media rule for the header and the header table, move the theme button out of the toolbar to the top of the body in the companion, docgen and fallback shells, and remove the docgen rule that cannot match; update the three shell tests; commit.

Add the live browser test, gated by INSRC_LIVE_TESTS=1 and the google-chrome binary, that renders a real ER companion page and a docgen page and checks them at desktop and 360px widths: light by default, a dark canvas with no white rim or strip after the switch, the switch fixed top right and clear of the header table at scroll zero, the header table fitting at 360px, and no font text at the top; keep the screenshots with the build record.

migration.backwardCompat: Pages already generated are static files and keep their old behaviour until regenerated; nothing reads them. The stored choice key and values are unchanged, so a reader's earlier choice still applies. The exported functions keep their signatures. The generated markup changes in five ways: the font-face rules now sit inside a style element in the head of every shell, the docgen shell's never-matching rule is removed, the companion page's theme root moves from a div to the body, the theme button moves to a direct child of the body, and the companion style gains a narrow-width media rule.

alternativesConsidered.name: Theme root moves to <body>; canvas by propagation; shared floating switch in pageCssFor
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Put class insrc-viewer and data-theme on <body> in the companion shell so its background propagates to the canvas, give the root a viewport-filling box with top clearance, wrap the font-face rules in a style tag, default to light, and float #iv-theme top right.
alternativesConsidered.approach: In the companion shell render <body class="insrc-viewer" data-theme="light" data-iv-export-css=...> with the existing div.page inside. Because the theme root is then the body and html has no background of its own, the body background propagates to the canvas, so no html rule and no :has() are needed. pageCssFor gives '.insrc-viewer' the surface background, box-sizing:border-box, min-height:100vh and padding-top:56px, and a '.insrc-viewer #iv-theme' rule: fixed, top:12px, right:12px, 32px round, with a z-index above the content. The companion structural CSS gets a max-width:480px media rule that stacks header.hdr and sets table.ref min-width:0 and width:100%. Wrap fontFaceCssForArtifacts() in a <style> tag inside pageStyleTags, drop the prefers-color-scheme fallback from viewerBootScript and the fallback shell's own script, and move #iv-theme to a direct child of the body in all three shells. Remove the docgen shell's never-matching '.insrc-viewer html,.insrc-viewer body' rule.
pros: One shared rule set fixes the surface and the switch in all three shells
No :has() or other newer selector: canvas propagation is core CSS
Matches how the docgen shells already work
cons: Touches four files and moves a button in three templates
The fallback shell keeps its own small script, so two mode-selection implementations stay in step by test

Add page CSS keyed on html[data-theme] that sets the html and body background and colour from the same tokens, and have applyMode set data-theme on document.documentElement as well as the root. Fix the font-face tag, the default and the button as in a1.
pros: The markup of the companion page is unchanged
Works for any future shell that wraps its content
cons: Two places hold the mode, so they can drift, and the tokens must be repeated for html
The never-matching layout rule still needs a separate fix
More CSS and script than a1
